accepted_findings: Theorem 2.1 and the public deterministic_chores statement agree for n >= 3: finite nonnegative atomless costs, all legal full-history ordinary Eval/Cut policies, complete exact chore EF, and both claimed query envelopes.

The concrete cost-independent program starts from empty history with no supplied cost cache. native_complete closes the population recursion using concrete_step_complete; only strictly smaller child populations are used.

Physical shares are pairwise disjoint and cover Icc 0 1 literally. Finite Ioc lists plus one uniquely owned singleton {0} give finite interval outputs; atomlessness preserves costs. Every piece endpoint is within [0,1] and inherited or an actual Cut reply.

capacity_bound proves the actual total query capacity, including n initial Evals, is at most both n^(3*n)*2^(27*n) and 2^(14*n*(Nat.clog 2 n+1)); successful trace length and Cut count inherit their minimum.

The formal fixed clearance length 14*n*weight n and explicit observer-recording/interpreter costs conservatively differ from the sharper manuscript auxiliary ledger. Appendix I explicitly discloses these choices and does not claim verbatim verification of every auxiliary estimate.
